title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier with a bounded automated repair budget increases the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator. For each intent a single shared LLM candidate was produced and evaluated under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (validator + ≤1 automated repair). Outcomes: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We archive preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts and interpret results with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational deployment policies.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent‑to‑configuration translation and automated repair. Operational pre‑deployment validation must guarantee semantic properties (sequencing, reachability, policy preservation) that go beyond syntactic correctness. A common engineering pattern pairs a generative model with a deterministic validator and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce operational risk. However, the measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends critically on what is held fixed (the estimand), the single‑shot quality of the generator, the validator's expressiveness, and the permitted repair budget.

We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) to quantify the deterministic rescue achievable when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. Our primary research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under a shared_initial estimand; (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle that includes validator traces and the single automated repair transcript; (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation of estimator conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps CI/CD pipelines.
sections.related_work: Prior work demonstrates rapid adoption of LLMs for network configuration tasks and recommends tooling that augments LLMs with external validators, planners, or repair modules [1]–[4]. Several recent system papers propose planner‑centric or ReAct‑style frameworks enabling LLMs to call external validators or simulators to coordinate multi‑step NetOps workflows [5], and empirical reports show that generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve surface correctness compared with unconstrained generation, though magnitude depends on validator coverage and dataset specifics [3],[1]. The literature also emphasizes the importance of clear estimand definitions: many prior evaluations conflate benefits from deterministic validation with benefits from resampling or iterative regeneration, complicating attribution of gains to the verifier alone [2],[4]. Finally, work on hallucination detection and deterministic safety nets highlights complementary detection and mitigation strategies but underlines that effectiveness is threat‑ and validator‑dependent [6]. Our study explicitly isolates the bounded deterministic rescue of a verifier+≤1‑repair pipeline under a shared_initial conditioning to provide an operationally meaningful bound for policies that restrict model calls.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The design was preregistered (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) and frozen before the main run. The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) computed on N = 300 paired intents after applying preregistered inclusion/exclusion rules. Analysis used a paired binary executor producing contingency counts (n11,n10,n01,n00), an exact two‑sided McNemar test, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000). The preregistration specified an optional pilot (n = 60) for discordance estimation that was not executed.

Task generation and stratification. Tasks were deterministically generated into a synthetic topology suite stratified by difficulty (low/medium/high) so that the confirmatory sample contains 100 pairs per stratum. Each task encodes: a natural‑language intent, initial and expected final device states, sequencing constraints (must_be_down_for_fields), preserve_unspecified_state invariants, and protected interfaces. Difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) determined stratum membership.

Shared_initial protocol and model configuration. To isolate deterministic verifier/repair rescue from resampling effects we implemented a shared_initial estimand: for each pair the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate with the declared generator gpt-5-mini; that identical candidate was reused for the baseline and guarded evaluations. The model configuration declared requested_model = "gpt-5-mini" and max_output_tokens configured to allow full configuration proposals.

Deterministic validator and bounded repair. Semantic evaluation used a deterministic validator implementing a full_intent_constraint_validation rule that checks sequencing invariants, required command counts, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability invariants encoded by the synthetic suite, and forbidden‑template protections for protected interfaces. Scoring is binary: an unflagged candidate counts as a pass. The guarded pipeline permits at most one automated repair attempt. The repair operator is a constrained, localized edit routine limited to sequencing and small insertion edits (for example, inserting a missing 'admin down' before a VLAN/MTU change); repaired candidates are re‑validated deterministically. Any candidate still flagged after the single permitted repair counts as a failure for the guarded condition.

Execution, contamination controls, and stopping rules. The run used an instrumented adapter that enforced the shared_initial generation per pair, the repair budget ≤1, and logged provider/audit metadata. Contamination controls included one negative control per stratum and automated invariant checks; pairs were excluded from confirmatory analysis only if both pipeline calls failed due to provider/infrastructure outage. The preregistered stopping rule—halt if >20% of attempted pairs were excluded due to dual‑call outages—did not trigger.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and integrity. The adapter completed the confirmatory run with 600 completed episodes (300 complete pairs) and 301 model calls used (300 shared_initial generations plus one repair invocation). Provider auditing recorded the single repair stage and no provider outages; deterministic reconciliation confirmed consistent episode accounting and that the shared_initial candidate was reused across conditions.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Binary scoring yielded baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 0.9966667, guarded = 1.0). The paired contingency counts were n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0, giving an absolute paired improvement of 0.0033333. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test on the discordant counts returned p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00,0.01]. Because discordance is minimal (m = 1), the exact test lacks power to detect small effects; the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point in this context.

Per‑stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Per stratum: low baseline 100/100 and guarded 100/100; medium baseline 100/100 and guarded 100/100; high baseline 99/100 and guarded 100/100. The single discordant pair occurred in the high stratum and invoked the permitted automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial failure to a sequencing omission (an omitted 'admin down' prior to a VLAN/MTU change). The constrained repair performed a single localized insertion of the missing sequencing command; after the edit the deterministic validator reported a pass. Thus the guarded pipeline produced a deterministic rescue in exactly one hard example at the cost of one additional repair invocation for the whole run.

Contamination, missingness, and cost. Contamination checks produced no flags; no episodes were excluded under preregistered rules. The guarded pipeline required one additional repair call across 300 pairs (model_calls_used = 301), indicating that bounded automated repair imposed negligible extra model‑call cost in this synthetic evaluation. All raw validator traces and the single repair transcript are archived in the run bundle for forensic inspection.
sections.discussion:
Estimand conditioning and operational meaning. The shared_initial estimand conditions on a single LLM draw per intent and models operational policies that limit model calls for cost, latency, or governance reasons. Under this estimand the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the identical generator output. Evaluations that permit resampling, verifier‑guided regeneration, or iterative interaction implement a different estimand and typically yield larger apparent benefits because they exploit generator variance; such workflows must be evaluated separately.

Ceiling effects, pilot omission, and inferential sensitivity. The baseline single‑shot generator achieved near ceiling performance (299/300) on the chosen synthetic suite, leaving minimal room for deterministic rescue and producing only one discordant pair. The preregistration described an optional calibration pilot for discordance estimation that was not executed; absent pilot calibration, the main run faced reduced sensitivity to detect small absolute differences. This outcome illustrates the practical value of small pilots when generator quality on the targeted task distribution is uncertain.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The single observed failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, ACL misconfigurations) were not observed at scale under this synthetic generator. The practical utility of a guarded pipeline depends on (i) the distribution of failure modes in deployment and (ii) validator expressiveness: richer validators that capture reachability or ACL semantics may increase observed rescue rates. Conversely, if operator policies disallow automated edits, deterministic validation remains useful primarily for detection and human escalation.

Repair budget tradeoffs and operational cost. We intentionally bounded repair to a single constrained edit to measure localized deterministic rescue; iterative repair, larger edit operators, or interactive verifier‑guided regeneration would increase rescue opportunities but change the estimand and model‑call budget. In our run the marginal model‑call cost for deterministic rescue was minimal (one extra call across 300 pairs), suggesting that bounded repair can be low‑cost under some operational constraints, but generalization requires evaluation across different task distributions and repair operator designs.

Implications for NetOps CI/CD. Organizations should align evaluation estimands with operational policies. When model calls are tightly budgeted, the shared_initial estimand yields an operationally meaningful bound on deterministic verifier/repair rescue for a single candidate. When pipelines permit resampling or interactive steering, evaluations should allow those modes to measure achievable success under that policy. The archived artifacts and per‑episode validator traces enable targeted follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, generator strength, task distribution, or repair budget.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation on 300 synthetic NetOps intents we compared a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) with accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate under a shared_initial estimand using gpt-5-mini. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). The guarded pipeline deterministically rescued one sequencing omission under the bounded repair budget. The near‑ceiling baseline constrains inferential sensitivity for small absolute improvements in this setting. We release full preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility and to guide follow‑up studies that change estimand conditioning, model budgets, or validator design.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
